properties.name: Approving a node never erases the record that someone authored it — a contributor's roles toward a node accumulate
properties.statement:
A contributor can stand in more than one relation to the same node — wrote it, reviewed it, signed it off — and each is a fact with its own date. Recording one must never displace another. The design's own word (dec:design-authorship-identity) is that authorship "is past tense and never changes"; a settling write that removed it broke that promise silently, and flo2 lost August authorship on two rules to September rulings before a diff happened to catch it.

The call surface a user or agent already knows stays as it is: `authored_by(role=…)`, and `approver` on the constructors and status setters. What changes is underneath: the stored relation carries the SET of roles and a date per role, and a write adds to it. A store or export written before this reads correctly and is brought to the new shape without anyone asking for it.

Anthony's word, 2026-09-14: "Go with (a), fix it at the root."
